t: A body is found in the river by the ford at Ashford: a stranger, throat cut, purse gone.
{who} is accused of witchcraft by a neighbor after a cow dies in the night.
Bandits from the woods raid {place} at dusk; {who} is beaten and robbed.
Fire breaks out at {place}; {fixture} burns before the buckets arrive.
A sickness comes in with a peddler: three households in {place} take to their beds.
{who} falls sick with the coughing fever and cannot work.
The lord's tax collector arrives a week early and seizes grain from the tithe barn.
A wolf takes a child from the edge of {place}. The valley wants blood.
{who} finds a purse of old coin buried under {fixture} at {place}.
A stranger at the inn offers good coin for anyone who will guide him through the forest road by night.
{who} and {who2} come to blows at the inn over a debt; {who} is hurt.
A wandering friar arrives at the chapel preaching the end of the world and the sin of hoarding grain.
The lord falls gravely ill. The steward rules in his name and nobody likes it.
The steward is caught with two sets of ledgers. He flees toward the east road with a chest of coin.
spawn: the steward's abandoned ledger room, chest gone

t: Freezing rain glazes the valley; the road east is closed for good this year.
A comet hangs over the castle for three nights. The pious call it a warning; the drunk call it luck.
A child is born to a family in {place}; the father is not who everyone thinks.
{who}'s roof gives way under the snow load in the night.
A deserter from the King's war hides in {place}, wounded, armed, and asking for silence.
Rats get into the grain loft at the mill; a week's flour is fouled.
{who} receives word that a relative has died and left them a plot of land in the next valley, if they can reach it before the snows.
A traveling merchant sets up at the market with salt, iron, and wine, and prices that insult everyone.
spawn: a traveling merchant with salt, iron, and wine

t: {who} is challenged to a fight at dawn by {who2} over an insult nobody else heard.
The well at Market town runs foul; someone says it was poisoned, someone says it was the frost.
{who} catches {who2} stealing from {fixture} at {place} after dark.
A bridge of ice forms over the ford and children dare each other to cross it.
The chapel bell cracks in the cold and will not ring again without a smith.
An old woman in {place} dies in her sleep and leaves behind a locked box nobody has the key to.
The lord announces a feast at the castle in three days and commands every household to send food.
{who} is offered marriage by a family with land, on terms that would shame them.
Wolves are seen on the forest road in daylight. Something has driven them from the deep woods.
A hunter finds a fresh grave in the forest with no marker.
spawn: an unmarked grave in the woods

t: {who} wakes with no memory of last night and blood on their sleeve that is not theirs.
The steward posts a notice: anyone found hoarding grain will be flogged at the market cross.
A miracle is claimed at the chapel: a blind girl says she can see. Pilgrims will come, and coin with them.
{who} is found drunk in the graveyard, digging.
A flood of meltwater takes out the footbridge at Millbrook.
A messenger from the next valley brings word that their harvest failed and they are coming to buy, or take, grain.
spawn: a messenger from the next valley, waiting for an answer

t: {who} is bitten by a dog that then dies foaming. Everyone steps back from them.
The inn's hidden stash of coin is found gone. Sten swears he never left the taproom.
A thaw opens the road east for one day only. Anyone leaving must go now.
{who} is named in a dying man's confession as the one who wronged him years ago.
A love letter meant for {who} is delivered to {who2} by mistake and read aloud at the inn.
spawn: a love letter, read by everyone

t: The miller's ledger goes missing from the grain loft. Every debtor in the valley breathes easier.
spawn: the empty shelf where the ledger was

t: A stone falls from the castle wall and kills a goat. The wall is worse than anyone admitted.
{who} inherits a debt: their dead father owed the moneylender, and the note has surfaced.
A troupe of players arrives at the inn and performs a play that is plainly about the steward. He is not amused.
A runaway serf from the lord's own fields begs sanctuary at the chapel.
{who} finds {who2}'s secret written on a scrap of paper tucked into the chapel's alms box.
An early blizzard shuts every road in the valley for the day. Nobody travels.
{who} is struck by a falling branch on the forest road and lies unconscious until found.
Three sheep are found slaughtered at Oakstead, not eaten, just killed. Not wolves.
The baker's ovens crack; there will be no bread in the market for three days.
The lord's son returns from the King's war with a scar, a temper, and an eye on somebody's wife.
